title: Enkidu: The Making of a Man
subtitle: From the herd to the city — what it costs to become human

learningObjectives.text: How is Enkidu drawn out of the wild?
What does he lose in becoming human?

change.work: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
change.author: Anonymous
change.translator: Morris Jastrow and Albert T. Clay
change.locator: Pennsylvania Tablet · Column III · part 1; Pennsylvania Tablet · Column III · part 1, normalized characters 115-785
change.excerpt: Enkidu had not known To eat food. To drink wine He had not been taught. The woman opened her mouth and Spoke to Enkidu: "Eat food, O Enkidu, The provender of life! Drink wine, the custom of the land!" Enkidu ate food Till he was satiated. Wine he drank, Seven goblets. His spirit was loosened, he became hilarious. His heart became glad and His face shone. [The barber(?)] removed The hair on his body. He was anointed with oil. He became manlike. He put on a garment, He was like a man. He took his weapon; Lions he attacked, (so that) the night shepherds could rest. He plunged the dagger; Lions he overcame. The great [shepherds] lay down; Enkidu was their protector.
change.note: Verbatim translation from the named Old Babylonian tablet witness in this edited edition. Brackets and question marks signal textual restoration or uncertainty.

narrativeBlocks.title: Wild as the steppe
narrativeBlocks.body: Enkidu runs with gazelles, drinks at the water-hole, and frees animals from hunters' traps — a man made of clay, innocent of everything human.

narrativeBlocks.title: The trap that works
narrativeBlocks.body: Hunters can't catch him, so they send Shamhat, a temple woman. Six days and seven nights with her do what no snare could: afterwards the gazelles flee from him. He has become human — and wild things sense it.

narrativeBlocks.title: The price of belonging
narrativeBlocks.body: Enkidu gains speech, cooked food, beer, clothing — and loses the herd. The epic is blunt about the trade: civilization is a door that closes behind you.

narrativeBlocks.title: To Uruk
narrativeBlocks.body: Shamhat brings him to the city — and on the road he hears of Gilgamesh's tyranny over brides. Enkidu's first act as a human is to oppose the king: the equal the gods designed has arrived angry.

narrativeBlocks.title: An older Eden
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the world's earliest 'civilization costs innocence' story — two millennia before Genesis, the same pattern: eat, become aware, and the wilderness no longer wants you.

quiz.prompt: How is Enkidu drawn from the wild?

choices.text: The temple woman Shamhat stays with him — afterwards the animals flee from him, and he is human
He wanders to Uruk out of curiosity

quiz.explanation: Civilization reaches him through intimacy, not force — and the wild rejects him instantly.

quiz.prompt: What does Enkidu lose by becoming human?

choices.text: His wild kin — the gazelles flee him, and he can never return to the herd

quiz.explanation: The epic prices civilization in lost kinship — the door closes behind him.
